As of the most recent evidence available, 2024 is set to be the hottest year on record, superseding 2023 [d5][d4]. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) reported in November 2024 that 2024 is on track to be the warmest year on record, with the January–September 2024 global mean surface air temperature at 1.54°C above the pre-industrial average [d4]. UN News confirmed in December 2024 that 2024 would become the hottest year on record, capping a decade of unprecedented heat fuelled by human activities [d5]. NPR similarly reported in December 2024 that 2024 is "almost certain to take over the top spot as the hottest year," unseating 2023 [d6]. Earlier in 2024, multiple high-credibility sources including NOAA, NASA, Copernicus, and WMO had identified 2023 as the hottest year on record since modern record-keeping began, at approximately 1.18°C–1.45°C above pre-industrial averages [d1][d2][d3][d7][d9], but this has since been overtaken by 2024 data.
